_what: Per-question decisions for the July-2023 P&E (Electrical Wing) General Studies import: keep-or-drop, which GS syllabus unit and leaf sub-topic it belongs to, and a one-line explanation of the keyed answer.
_split_policy: The user asked for STATIC GK only. `drop` marks a question whose value depends on when it is asked - an office holder, an annual figure, a 'recently'/'is planning to' framing, one year's award or election result. Nothing is silently discarded: every dropped question keeps its reason here and the importer prints them all on every run, so pulling one back is a one-field edit.
_this_paper_is_the_current_affairs_heavy: The Oct-2025 sitting lost 7 of 100 to this policy. This one loses 21 - 17 as time-bound and 4 as off-syllabus - because its first 45 questions are largely a 2023 news quiz - a Foxconn investment plan, a May-2023 EU fine, an RBI surplus transfer, a kit sponsorship, a budget line. That is a fact about the paper, not a failure of the import: the Commission front-loads current affairs and this sitting was set in July 2023.
_unit_9_is_open_to_static_questions_and_: The Oct-2025 entry recorded that the 12-mark Current Affairs unit 'stays authored-only on purpose'. That rule is kept where it bites - no stale news is imported - but it is NOT read as 'no past-paper question may ever carry a unit-9 tag'. The bank's own 10 authored unit-9 questions are all static ('The Bharat Ratna may be conferred for', 'World Environment Day is observed annually on which date?'), and the Oct-2025 drop records themselves carry unit-9 tags. So a permanent fact that happens to live in a current-affairs category - the Quad's membership, who wrote 'A Long Walk to Freedom', that the 2023 G7 met at Hiroshima - is kept and tagged there. Dropping Q98 ('When do we observe World Population Day?') while the bank keeps an authored twin about World Environment Day would have been incoherent.
_off_syllabus_note: Four questions are dropped for having no leaf anywhere in the GS syllabus rather than for going stale: Q28 (the Latin expansion of LL.B), Q72 (the currency of Japan), Q76 (a bank's marketing slogan) and Q82 (a perfect-square word problem). Q82 is the Q78-of-this-batch: unit 10 is plainly the right unit, but its leaves are percentage/ratio, average/profit-loss, interest, series, coding, syllogism, seating - and n squared minus 111 = 10914 is none of them. Tagging it to a percentage leaf would send by-topic revision to the wrong place, which is the mis-tagging bug of 2026-09-04. Q85 is kept by the same test read the other way: a bell ringing at 45-minute intervals is time arithmetic, so the 'Time and work, time speed distance' leaf is the right family even though clocks are not named in it.
_key_quality: The key is dated 8 September 2023 - three days after the 5 September key for the same exam's Electrical/CSE/Mechanical papers, so General Studies was finalised separately. It holds up. The 14 answers most worth doubting - the Mizoram-specific ones, the award and 'first' claims, and the ones where 'largest' is ambiguous - were checked against independent sources and every one came back correct, so unlike ILM2023 (12 wrong in 135) and MES2023 (8 in 62) this batch needs no correction annotations at all. Five carry a caveat rather than a correction, on the card itself: Q49 (the Chenab is largest by discharge, but the Sutlej is longer and has the bigger basin - the key follows NCERT's convention), Q36 (three mega-cities is the census-2011 figure; Bengaluru and Chennai have since passed 10 million), Q60 (NHPC was incorporated in 1975 but is no longer hydro-only), Q54 (Kandla was renamed Deendayal Port in 2017) and Q8. Q8 is the one to distrust: the claim that JC Lalnunsanga is the first Mizo Advocate-on-Record traces only to his own firm's site and an affiliated post - no court record or independent report. It is kept because MPSC keyed it and the alternatives are implausible, but the card says so plainly.
